For Ansonia specifically, it means this: if enough registered Democrats here sign, it allows a contested Democratic primary for this House seat to appear on the ballot.

It doesn’t change any laws, it doesn’t take a position on any issue, and it doesn’t commit you or anyone else to support any candidate. It only determines whether Ansonia voters get that option or not.

I will say this, though. I spent time in Ansonia last August and September, walking Main Street while Cassetti was still mayor. What stood out to me was both the strength of the Valley’s manufacturing infrastructure and the number of young families moving in, many from New York.

We invested for decades to build the systems that move goods in and out of the Valley, and we shouldn’t abandon that now. Helping those families become long-term residents matters.

I won’t go further into that here, because this isn’t a campaign yet. But I do see Ansonia and the Valley as a central part of Connecticut’s future.
